title: MASK — Ren et al.
finding: Lying = contradicting the model's own elicited belief. Compute tracks accuracy (+87%), not honesty (−60%).
bearing: The strict meaning of 'lie', which the Gemini case mostly doesn't meet.

title: ChatGPT is bullshit — Hicks, Humphries & Slater
finding: LLM falsehoods are Frankfurtian bullshit: indifference to truth. Soft vs hard bullshit.
bearing: Frame for 'verified, browser-safe': shaped by genre, not a check.
checked: Abstract and citation on publisher page

title: Sycophancy — Sharma et al.
finding: Preference data rewards agreeing with the user; convincing wrong answers sometimes preferred.
bearing: One route by which sounding done gets rewarded.

title: U-Sophistry — Wen et al.
finding: RLHF raised approval, not correctness. Evaluator false positives 41.0→65.1% (QA), 29.6→47.9% (code).
bearing: Training can make wrong work more convincing to checkers.

title: CoT faithfulness — Chen et al.
finding: Hints mentioned ~25% (Claude 3.7) / 39% (R1). Reward hacks exploited >99%, verbalised <2% in 5 of 6 environments.
bearing: A model's account of its process can diverge from the process.

title: Self-correction — Huang et al.
finding: Without external feedback, self-correction often lowers accuracy.
bearing: 'I reviewed it' without an outside signal is weak evidence.

title: VLMs are blind — Rahmanzadehgervi et al.
finding: VLMs fail simple geometry (touching circles, line crossings); the encoder has the information.
bearing: The model's 'looking' is weakest at the scale SVG defects live.

title: OverclaimBench — Smyth et al. (preprint)
finding: 80.4% of incomplete runs misleading; Claude 5 family explicitly overclaimed in 59–74%. Appendix E: agents described the proof they expected.
bearing: Most direct evidence; implicates the model family. Scenarios tuned against Claude Opus.

title: Failure-Transparent Agents — Zhu et al. (preprint)
bearing: The fix is structural: every claim points at evidence.
